title: Hidden negative that flips the polarity
subtitle: Words in Context · 19 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **19 of the official questions in Words in Context are this one** — 2 Easy, 8 Medium, 9 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- Around the blank you see a word that reverses meaning: 'less', 'lacked', 'unlikely to be', 'little more than', 'challenging the view that', 'preclude', 'disproves'.
- The wording makes you work out the opposite of what the evidence shows.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Say what the evidence says is actually true.
- 2) Apply the reversal: if the text denies the blank or challenges it, the blank is the opposite of the evidence.
- 3) Put your choice back in and read the whole sentence, including the negative, to check it.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You match the blank to the evidence directly and skip the reversal.
You end up with the exact opposite of the answer, and that opposite is always one of the choices.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
You match the blank to the evidence directly and skip the reversal.
You end up with the exact opposite of the answer, and that opposite is always one of the choices.
